compatSex.setupDesc: Twenty questions about desire, tenderness, how you talk about it, trying new things and the right moment. You each answer on your own, and your answers only show up at the end.
compatSex.avertissement: Adults only. There's no right answer: answer for yourself, not to please your partner.
compatSex.relaisDebut: Answer without your partner seeing the screen.
compatSex.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Pass the phone: their answers stay hidden until the result.
compatSex.verdictLoin: Not the same... Want to talk about it?
compatSex.parlerTitre: Where there's the most to talk about
compatSex.toutTitre: All your answers, side by side
compatSex.axe_envie_fort: You want it about as much, and about as often. That's often the point that creates the most tension in a couple, and for you it's settled.
compatSex.axe_tendresse_fort: You expect the same thing when it comes to tenderness: cuddles, taking your time, the moments after. You feel it every day, not just in bed.
compatSex.axe_parole_fort: You talk about it the same way, and that's what makes everything else work. When you can tell each other what you like, the rest falls into place.
compatSex.axe_audace_fort: You have the same appetite for new things, whether that means trying them or sticking with what works. Nobody pushes the other where they don't want to go.
compatSex.axe_rythme_fort: You agree on the right moment and on who makes the first move. That means a lot fewer misunderstandings, like "you're never in the mood".
compatSex.axe_envie_parler: You don't want it quite as much, or quite as often. It's very common, and it's easier to sort out by talking than by keeping count. To get the conversation going: "What would an ideal week look like for you?"
compatSex.axe_tendresse_parler: You don't expect the same thing when it comes to tenderness: one of you needs more time, cuddles or gentleness than the other. A simple question to start: "What makes you feel loved, outside the bedroom?"
compatSex.axe_parole_parler: You don't talk about sex with the same ease. That's fine, but it's often where everything starts getting better. To ease into it, each of you can name one thing you already love before talking about what you'd like.
compatSex.axe_audace_parler: You don't have the same appetite for new things: one of you would like to try, the other prefers what they know. The easiest way is to talk about it calmly, outside the bedroom, with both of you free to say no without explaining why.
compatSex.axe_rythme_parler: You don't agree on the right moment or on who makes the first move, and that quickly leads to misunderstandings. Just ask each other what time of day you feel like it most, the answer is often a surprise.
compatSex.r1_d: Your answers are far apart on a lot of questions. That doesn't mean it can't work between you: sexual compatibility changes a lot over time, especially when you talk about it. Look at your biggest gaps below, and talk about them calmly, without trying to decide who's right.
compatSex.r2_d: You meet on some points and you're far apart on others. That's the case for a lot of couples. The most useful thing is to start with the dimension where the gap is biggest, and talk about it before it turns into frustration.
compatSex.r3_d: Your desires go the same way on most questions. There are a few gaps left, and that's normal, nobody wants exactly the same things as their partner. It's often the small gaps nobody talks about that end up weighing the most.
compatSex.r4_d: Your desires meet almost everywhere: wanting it, tenderness, how you talk about it. The few gaps left are good things to talk about rather than problems.
compatSex.r5_d: Your answers are almost all alike, and that's rare! Keep the habit of talking to each other: desires change over time, and talking is how you stay this close.
